trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival – Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Amsterdam Centraal train from Schiphol Airport (€5.40 single, ~17 min). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam and drop off luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Self-guided canal walk along the Herengracht and Prinsengracht from your hotel. Stroll the iconic 17th-century merchant houses, cross the famous Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge), and get your bearings in the Jordaan neighbourhood. Free of charge and a perfect gentle introduction after a flight.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Leidseplein and Koningsplein squares nearby. Browse the floating Bloemenmarkt (flower market stalls may be closing but the area is scenic). Grab a budget dinner in the Jordaan neighbourhood.

meals.breakfast: Grab a sandwich or stroopwafel at Schiphol Airport before landing (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Pick up a broodje (Dutch sandwich) from Broodje Bert or a local bakery near Centraal Station (~€4–6).
meals.dinner: Moeders restaurant in the Jordaan for hearty Dutch stamppot from ~€14, or grab a cone of patatje oorlog (fries with peanut sauce) from a street frietkot for ~€3–4.

day_by_day.notes: Get an OV-chipkaart (public transport card) at Schiphol or Centraal Station for easy tram/metro travel all week (~€7.50 deposit + top-up). Pre-book Anne Frank House tickets online as they sell out weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit – Open from 09:00. Arrive early to beat weekend crowds. Explore the Netherlands' premier art and history museum, home to Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' and Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid'. Budget tip: book tickets online in advance at €22.50 per adult to avoid queues. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Van Gogh Museum Experience – the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works including 'Sunflowers' and 'The Bedroom'. Tickets ~€22 (book online). Spend 1.5–2 hours. Afterwards, relax in the free Vondelpark just across the road — bring a snack and enjoy the green space popular with locals.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the city centre via tram. Walk along the Leidsegracht canal at dusk for golden-hour photos. Explore the Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes) boutique area for window shopping before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Albert Heijn supermarket grab-and-go: yoghurt, fruit, and a coffee (~€3–5). Many branches open by 08:00.
meals.lunch: Museumplein food trucks or Vondelpark café — a simple broodje or wrap (~€5–7).
meals.dinner: Foodhallen in the Oud-West district (10-min tram): an indoor food market with global street food stalls from ~€8–12 per dish. Very popular and budget-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday museums can be busy — arrive at Rijksmuseum right at 09:00. Both museums require timed entry tickets booked online. Combined museum spend ~€44–45; consider the Museumkaart (€69.90/year) if you plan 4+ museums — it pays off quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour – Timed entry slots often start from 09:00. Walk through the historic hiding place of Anne Frank and her family during World War II. A deeply moving and essential Amsterdam experience. Tickets ~€16 (must be booked weeks in advance online). Located a short walk from Canal House Amsterdam along the Prinsengracht.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, explore the surrounding Jordaan neighbourhood on foot — Amsterdam's most charming district with narrow lanes, independent galleries, and courtyard gardens (hofjes). Visit the free Westerkerk church (tower climb ~€9 for panoramic views, optional). Browse the Sunday Noordermarkt organic farmers' market (free entry, runs until ~16:00).
day_by_day.evening: Take tram 2 or 12 to the NDSM Wharf in Amsterdam Noord via a free ferry from Centraal Station for a cool industrial arts scene. Or stay local and enjoy a canal-side evening stroll along Brouwersgracht, one of Amsterdam's most photogenic canals, before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Winkel 43 on Noordermarkt — famous for apple pie (~€4) and coffee (~€3). A Jordaan institution.
meals.lunch: Noordermarkt Sunday market — fresh stroopwafels, herring sandwiches, cheese samples (~€5–8 self-curated).
meals.dinner: Tomaz restaurant in the Jordaan for affordable Dutch-European dishes (~€12–16), or pick up a döner kebab from a local snackbar for ~€6–7.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House is the single most important booking of the trip — if you haven't pre-booked, check for last-minute releases at 09:00 on the day. The Jordaan is very walkable from Canal House Amsterdam — no transport needed for most of today.

day_by_day.morning: Private Canal Boat Tour – Cruise Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal network on a guided boat tour, passing iconic 17th-century merchant houses, the Amstel River, and hidden waterways. Departs from various central piers (e.g., near Centraal Station or Leidseplein). Budget tip: opt for a shared group canal cruise (~€15–18) instead of private for significant savings, or book the listed private tour if budget allows. Duration ~1–1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Amsterdam Museum of the Canals (Huis Lachende Brug) or explore the Jewish Historical Museum quarter (~€17, or free with Museumkaart). Walk through Waterlooplein flea market (free entry) for vintage finds and souvenirs. Cross the Magere Brug on foot and walk along the Amstel riverbank.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the free FOAM Photography Museum courtyard area or simply wander the lit canal belt after dark — Amsterdam's canal ring is especially beautiful in the evening with reflections on the water. Grab a nightcap at a traditional Dutch brown café (bruine kroeg).

meals.breakfast: In-hotel or grab fresh bread and cheese from an Albert Heijn supermarket (~€3–5).
meals.lunch: Grab a raw herring (haring) sandwich from a street herring cart near Centraal Station — an authentic Dutch experience for ~€3–4.
meals.dinner: Kantjil & de Tijger for Indonesian rijsttafel (rice table) — a Dutch-colonial tradition, sharing plates from ~€18–22 per person. Very filling and worth the splurge.

day_by_day.notes: For the canal tour, shared 'hop-on hop-off' canal buses (~€26/day) are also an option if you want flexible afternoon canal access. Book the canal boat in advance on weekdays as popular morning slots fill up. Waterlooplein flea market is closed Sundays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the free Begijnhof — a hidden medieval courtyard with historic houses and a chapel, one of Amsterdam's best-kept secrets, just off the Spui square. Then explore the Amsterdam City Archives (Stadsarchief) building, free to enter, with rotating historical exhibitions. Walk through the Spui literary square and browse the Tuesday book market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final canal district exploration — rent a pedal boat or kayak on the Amstel (~€10–15/hour) for a DIY water experience, or walk the full Grachtengordel (canal ring) circuit. Visit the free Artis Royal Zoo gardens entrance area or the Hortus Botanicus garden (~€11) for a peaceful green farewell to the city. Do any last souvenir shopping at the Albert Cuyp Market (free entry, closes ~17:00).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and a walk along the illuminated canals. Head back to pack and prepare for departure. If flying the next morning, confirm Schiphol train times (trains run 24 hours, ~17 min to airport).

meals.breakfast: Café de Jaren on the Amstel — a grand café with a sunny terrace, coffee and pastry from ~€5–7.
meals.lunch: Albert Cuyp Market street food — stroopwafels, poffertjes (mini pancakes), fresh fruit (~€4–6 total).
meals.dinner: De Blauwe Hollander near Leidseplein for classic Dutch erwtensoep (split pea soup) and stamppot from ~€12–15. A cosy, authentic farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your OV-chipkaart topped up for the airport return journey. Budget summary estimate for 5 days: accommodation (variable), museum entry ~€60–80, transport ~€20–25, food ~€30–40/day eating a mix of street food and sit-down meals. Total estimated trip spend excluding flights: €300–420 per person for a comfortable budget experience.

trip_options.title: Classic Amsterdam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Schiphol to Centraal Station, ~17 min, €5) then a short taxi or tram to Canal House Amsterdam. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon Canal Stroll & Jordaan Orientation: After settling in, take a self-guided walk along the Herengracht and Prinsengracht canals near the hotel. Admire the iconic 17th-century merchant houses, flower boxes, and houseboats. Stop by the Westerkerk tower area for a classic Amsterdam view — a gentle, low-key introduction to the city with no advance booking needed.
day_by_day.evening: Private Canal Boat Tour: Book an early-evening slot (typically 17:00–19:00) on a guided private canal boat tour. Glide through the UNESCO-listed canal ring at golden hour, passing the Anne Frank House exterior, the Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge), and illuminated gabled facades. A perfect way to see the city after a travel day without too much walking.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and stroopwafel at Schiphol Airport before landing, or a light snack from the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Café Papeneiland (Prinsengracht 2) — a historic Amsterdam brown café serving Dutch uitsmijter (open-faced egg sandwiches) and hearty soups. Budget ~€12–16 per person.
meals.dinner: Brouwerij 't IJ Tasting Room & Café — enjoy craft beers brewed in a windmill with simple, satisfying bar food (bitterballen, cheese boards). Casual, mid-range, and quintessentially Amsterdam. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep it light. Pre-book the private canal boat tour in advance as evening slots sell out quickly, especially on weekends. Carry your passport for hotel check-in. The Canal House Amsterdam is ideally located in the Jordaan/canal ring area, making the afternoon walk and canal tour very accessible on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit (09:00–12:30): Start early at the Netherlands' premier art and history museum. Marvel at Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and Delftware collections. Pre-book timed entry tickets online (€22.50 adults) to avoid queues. Spend at least 2.5–3 hours to cover the highlights without rushing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience (13:30–16:30): Just a 5-minute walk from the Rijksmuseum, dive into the world's largest Van Gogh collection. See 'Sunflowers,' 'The Bedroom,' and 'Almond Blossom' in chronological context. Timed tickets required (€22 adults) — book well in advance as this is one of Amsterdam's most popular attractions. Afterward, relax in the adjacent Vondelpark.
day_by_day.evening: Vondelpark & Leidseplein Evening: Wind down with a stroll through Vondelpark (Amsterdam's beloved green lung), then head to the lively Leidseplein square for people-watching, street performers, and a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby Café Winkel 43 (Noordermarkt) — famous for its apple pie and fresh coffee. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Foodhallen Amsterdam (Bellamyplein 51) — an indoor food market near the museum quarter with diverse stalls (Vietnamese, Dutch, pizza, sushi). Perfect mid-range lunch stop. Budget ~€12–18.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Blauw (Amstelveenseweg 158) — celebrated Indonesian rijsttafel (rice table) experience, reflecting Amsterdam's colonial history. Vegetarian options available. Budget ~€28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book both museum tickets at least 2–3 weeks ahead — they frequently sell out, especially on Sundays. Wear comfortable shoes as you'll cover significant ground between museums. The tram (Line 2 or 12) connects the canal house area to the museum quarter in about 10 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour (09:00–11:30): One of Amsterdam's most emotionally significant sites. Walk through the secret annex where Anne Frank and her family hid for over two years. The audio guide (included) is narrated using Anne's own diary entries. Timed tickets are mandatory and must be booked weeks in advance (€16 adults). The experience is deeply moving — allow time to reflect afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk (13:00–16:30): Explore Amsterdam's most charming neighborhood on a guided food and culture walk. Wander through the Jordaan's narrow streets, visit the famous Albert Cuyp Market (though note: Albert Cuyp is in De Pijp — the Jordaan's own Noordermarkt is open Mondays for antiques). Sample Dutch cheeses, herring, stroopwafels, and jenever (Dutch gin). Discover hidden courtyards (hofjes) and independent boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Canal-Side Sunset Walk & Cocktails: Stroll along the Brouwersgracht (considered Amsterdam's most beautiful canal) at dusk. Stop at a canal-side terrace bar such as Café de Vergulde Gaper or Vesper Bar for craft cocktails and views.

meals.breakfast: Bakkerij Mediterranée (Haarlemmerdijk) — artisan bakery with fresh croissants, sourdough, and excellent coffee. Budget ~€7–10.
meals.lunch: Buffet van Odette (Prinsengracht 598) — charming lunch spot with homemade soups, quiches, and salads in a cozy canal-house setting. Budget ~€14–20.
meals.dinner: De Reiger (Nieuwe Leliestraat 34) — beloved Jordaan neighborhood bistro with a seasonal Dutch-French menu. Cozy, unpretentious, and mid-range. Reservations recommended. Budget ~€28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets are the hardest to secure in Amsterdam — book as early as possible (they release tickets 2 months ahead at 09:00 Amsterdam time). If tickets are unavailable, check for same-day queue releases at 09:00. The Jordaan walk and Anne Frank House are both within easy walking distance of Canal House Amsterdam.

day_by_day.morning: Amsterdam Canal Museum & Houseboat Museum (09:30–12:00): Explore the Amsterdam Museum of the Canals (Het Grachtenhuis) on Herengracht to understand how the city's iconic canal ring was engineered and built in the 17th century. Then visit the nearby Woonbootmuseum (Houseboat Museum) — a real 1914 houseboat converted into a fascinating exhibit about life on the water. Tickets are affordable (€6–9 each).
day_by_day.afternoon: Bicycle Canal Tour (13:00–16:00): Rent bikes from a nearby shop (€12–15/day) and cycle the full canal ring — Herengracht, Keizersgracht, and Prinsengracht — at your own pace. This is the most authentic Amsterdam experience. Stop at the Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge) over the Amstel River, and pedal through the De Pijp neighborhood to visit the Albert Cuyp Market for fresh stroopwafels and Dutch snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Classical Concert at the Concertgebouw or Jazz at Bimhuis: For a cultured evening, catch a performance at the world-famous Concertgebouw (mid-range tickets from €25–60) or opt for live jazz at Bimhuis, Amsterdam's premier jazz venue on the waterfront. Both offer memorable evenings without breaking the budget.

meals.breakfast: Scandinavian Embassy (Sarphatipark 34) — minimalist café known for exceptional specialty coffee and open-faced smørrebrød-style toasts. Budget ~€10–14.
meals.lunch: Albert Cuyp Market street food — try fresh Dutch herring (haring met uitjes), stroopwafels warm off the iron, and Surinamese roti. Budget ~€8–12 for a satisfying market lunch.
meals.dinner: Rijsel (Marcusstraat 52) — a former school gymnasium turned beloved brasserie, serving roast chicken and Belgian-inspired dishes. Lively atmosphere, excellent value. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cycling in Amsterdam is safe and intuitive — follow the dedicated bike lanes and obey traffic signals. Lock your bike securely at all times. If weather is poor (May can bring light rain), substitute the bike tour with a tram-based city loop or visit the Stedelijk Museum (modern art) as an indoor alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Begijnhof & Amsterdam City Center Hidden Gems (09:00–11:30): Discover the Begijnhof, a serene medieval courtyard hidden in the heart of Amsterdam — one of the city's best-kept secrets and free to enter. Nearby, explore the Amsterdam Museum passage and the Spui square. Then browse the famous Bloemenmarkt (floating flower market) on the Singel canal for tulip bulbs and Dutch souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: NEMO Science Museum & Eastern Docklands Walk (13:00–16:30): Visit NEMO, the striking green copper-hulled science museum designed by Renzo Piano. The rooftop terrace offers one of the best free panoramic views of Amsterdam's rooftops and harbor (rooftop access is free even without a museum ticket). Afterward, stroll through the Eastern Docklands (Java Island, Borneo Island) to see Amsterdam's innovative modern architecture alongside historic waterways.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Canal Dinner & Departure Prep: Enjoy a leisurely final dinner at a canal-side restaurant, then return to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure. Take a last evening walk along the Prinsengracht to soak in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Brecht (Weteringschans 157) — a cozy literary café with excellent coffee, eggs, and Dutch pastries. Budget ~€10–14.
meals.lunch: Gartine (Taksteeg 7) — a hidden gem tearoom near the Begijnhof serving homemade sandwiches, soups, and cakes using garden-grown ingredients. Intimate and mid-range. Budget ~€14–20. Reservations recommended.
meals.dinner: Greetje (Peperstraat 23) — Amsterdam's finest modern Dutch cuisine restaurant, celebrating local seasonal ingredients with creative flair. A fitting farewell dinner. Budget ~€38–50 per person including a glass of Dutch wine.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is in the evening. The Bloemenmarkt is best visited early before crowds arrive. NEMO rooftop is especially lovely on a clear May afternoon. Keep transit cards topped up for tram/metro to Schiphol on departure day (journey ~17 min from Centraal Station).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight KL lands at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from Amsterdam Airport Schiphol to Canal House Amsterdam via private luxury car transfer (~20 minutes). Settle into your elegantly appointed canal-view suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour: After freshening up, embark on a bespoke private canal boat tour departing from a dock steps from the hotel. Glide along the UNESCO-listed Grachtengordel, passing the Golden Bend, Westerkerk, and iconic 17th-century merchant houses. Your private guide will narrate the city's rich history while you sip chilled champagne on board. Duration: approximately 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Jordaan Neighborhood Evening Stroll & Dinner: Take a leisurely walk through the picturesque Jordaan district as the golden hour light reflects off the canals. Enjoy dinner at Restaurant Vinkeles, a Michelin-starred gem set inside a historic Dutch Reformed bakery, offering refined French-Dutch cuisine with an exceptional wine list.

meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by Canal House Amsterdam upon arrival — artisan cheeses, charcuterie, and fresh bread served in your suite
meals.dinner: Restaurant Vinkeles (Michelin-starred) — tasting menu with wine pairing; reserve the chef's table for an immersive culinary experience

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with your hotel concierge before travel. Book the private canal boat tour in advance as afternoon slots fill quickly. Confirm dinner reservation at Vinkeles well ahead — it is one of Amsterdam's most sought-after tables.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit: Begin the day with a sumptuous breakfast at the hotel, then head to the Rijksmuseum — the Netherlands' premier museum of art and history. Arrange a private guided tour (2–2.5 hours) to explore masterpieces by Rembrandt, Vermeer, and Frans Hals in depth, bypassing general queues with priority access. Don't miss the Night Watch and the Delftware gallery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience: A short walk from the Rijksmuseum, immerse yourself in the world's largest Van Gogh collection. With a timed priority-entry ticket, explore Sunflowers, The Bedroom, and the emotionally powerful letters to Theo. The museum's chronological layout offers a deeply personal journey through the artist's life. Afterward, relax with coffee at the museum's refined café overlooking Museumplein.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails & Fine Dining in De Pijp: Head to the fashionable De Pijp district for pre-dinner cocktails at Bar Oldenhof, a beautifully designed art deco bar. Dinner at Bolenius, a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant championing Dutch seasonal ingredients with creative, elegant presentations.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — fresh pastries, smoked salmon, Dutch cheeses, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Grand Café Rijksmuseum or a curated picnic from a premium deli on Museumplein — artisan sandwiches, seasonal salads, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Bolenius Restaurant — seasonal Dutch tasting menu with optional wine or juice pairing; book the kitchen-view table for an elevated experience

day_by_day.notes: Both museums are within walking distance of each other on Museumplein. Pre-book private guided tours and timed entries well in advance, especially for weekends. Consider a Museum Card if planning additional museum visits later in the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour: Begin with a mindful, early-morning visit to the Anne Frank House — one of the most profound historical sites in Europe. A privately guided or premium early-access slot allows you to move through the secret annex with space and quiet reflection before larger crowds arrive. The experience is deeply moving and essential to understanding Amsterdam's wartime history. Duration: approximately 1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk: Transition from reflection to discovery with a curated food and culture walk through the Jordaan — Amsterdam's most charming and storied neighborhood. Visit the famous Albert Cuyp Market area, browse independent galleries, stop at specialty cheese shops like De Kaaskamer, and sample Dutch stroopwafels, raw herring, and artisan chocolates with your expert local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Canal-Side Aperitivo & Dinner: Wind down with drinks on a private canal terrace at Brouwerij 't IJ (Amsterdam's iconic windmill brewery) or opt for a refined aperitivo at Hotel De L'Europe's Brasserie. Dinner at Spectrum (Seven Seas Restaurant) inside the Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam — a Michelin-starred experience set across a row of restored 17th-century canal houses.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Dignita Hoftuin — a beautiful garden café near the Jordaan serving organic, seasonal morning dishes including Dutch pancakes and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Curated tastings during the Jordaan Food & Culture Walk — herring, local cheeses, fresh stroopwafels, and seasonal market bites
meals.dinner: Spectrum at Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam — multi-course Michelin-starred tasting menu; request a canal-view table when booking

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House timed tickets must be booked months in advance — they sell out extremely quickly. Sunday mornings offer a quieter Jordaan experience. The Waldorf Astoria is a short taxi or canal bike ride from Canal House Amsterdam.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive Art Gallery & Antique District Tour: Spend a leisurely morning exploring Amsterdam's Spiegelkwartier (Mirror Quarter) — the city's prestigious antique and fine art district along Nieuwe Spiegelstraat. Browse galleries featuring Old Dutch Masters, Delftware, and rare antiquities. Arrange a private art consultant to curate the experience if interested in acquiring a piece. Afterward, visit the Hermitage Amsterdam or the Foam Photography Museum for a curated cultural interlude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Second Private Canal Boat Experience — Hidden Waterways: Return to the canals, this time exploring Amsterdam's lesser-known eastern islands and harbor waterways on a second private boat excursion. Sail past the striking NEMO Science Museum, the historic Scheepvaarthuis, and the wooden sailing ships moored at the Maritime Museum. Enjoy a private on-board lunch with Dutch bitterballen, smoked eel, and chilled white wine.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury Spa & Gourmet Dinner: Treat yourself to an early-evening wellness session at the Spa at Conservatorium Hotel — one of Amsterdam's finest luxury spas offering thermal baths, steam rooms, and bespoke treatments. Follow with dinner at Ciel Bleu on the 23rd floor of Hotel Okura Amsterdam — a two-Michelin-starred restaurant with sweeping panoramic city views and an extraordinary French-Japanese tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — freshly baked croissants, seasonal fruit, Dutch cold cuts, and barista-prepared coffee delivered to your canal-view suite
